newsitem.title: UK: LIFFE sees 200-300 mln stg potential cost for site.
newsitem.headline: LIFFE sees 200-300 mln stg potential cost for site.

text.p: LIFFE's potential investment to develop a new trading floor and office complex at the edge of London's financial district could be in the 200-300 million stg range, LIFFE chief executive Daniel Hodson said.

"We're talking about a sort of development which could be in the order of 200-300 million pounds but it does depend very much on the specification," Hodson told Reuters in an interview. "It also depends very much on the method by which we fund it."
LIFFE, the London International Financial Futures and Options Exchange, said late last year it reached agreement with Spitalfields Developments Limited to buy a site.

Terms of the deal were not disclosed but LIFFE chose the site over five other locations including the Canary Wharf complex in London's docklands area. The agreement allows LIFFE to sell the site to London's City Corporation if it decided not to proceed at any time prior to December 31, 2001.
Spitalfields is an old market site on the edge of London's financial district and next to London's working class East End.

LIFFE, which is bracing for the possibility of volume growth in the coming years, also is looking at the potential benefits of consolidating its sprawling group of sites in London, which comprises seven offices and three trading floors.
"It could well make sense from a financial point of view to consolidate there anyway," Hodson said.

"None of these things has been decided -- what ultimately the building would look like, whether we build it ourselves or whether a developer builds it, whether a funder is involved to buy the finished buioding from us or the developer," he said.
Hodson said traditionally LIFFE has been unwilling to borrow.
"We did raise some bank lines for this building (at Cannon Bridge) but by culture I think the members are very unkeen to create excessive future obligations on their successors.

"The board has usually in the past been much happier to build up reserves to meet future outgoings rather than borrow in anticipation of them, bearing in mind this is something which will be financed over a long period of time," he said.
